items.title: Decade after Praja Sankalpa Yatra, YSRCP chief Jagan announces another march in 2027
items.summary: YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Andhra Pradesh chief minister YS Jagan Mohan Reddy has announced a statewide padayatra in September or October of 2027. Scheduled two years ahead of the next Assembly elections, the padayatra is expected to strengthen the party’s grassroots organisation and help it return to power in 2029. Addressing YSRCP leaders, elected representatives and key functionaries from the Parchur Assembly constituency at the party’s central office in Vijayawada on Wednesday, September 9, Jagan called on the cadre to prepare for the upcoming local body elections. He described them as a test of the party’s organisational strength. The proposed padayatra comes nearly a decade after Jagan’s 3,648-km Praja Sankalpa Yatra, which began in November 2017 and continued for 341 days across Andhra Pradesh. He travelled through 13 districts and 134 Assembly constituencies, meeting people and holding public meetings as he positioned himself as an alternative to Telugu Desam Party’s N Chandrababu Naidu. items.title: Madhya Pradesh High Court slams its IT wing for non-functional website; directs audit by TCS, Infosys, L&T
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court has ordered action against its Information Technology wing (IT wing) staff over repeated glitches in the court's website, which was hampering the Court's functioning, particularly e-hearing. In an order passed on September 8, a bench of Justices Vivek Agarwal and Avanindra Kumar Singh noted that the condition of the website was far from satisfactory and the Court's judicial time was being wasted due to the incompetence of the IT staff. Hence, it directed the Chief Justice to take action against the concerned IT staff. "The High Court Website is not support e-hearing. There are several glitches in the website. We have requested Mr. KS Kushwaha, Registrar (ITCSA) to assist us. He is reported to be on his way to the Court. However, we take a very serious view that our judicial time has been wasted due to incompetency of the IT staff. Let Hon'ble the Chief Justice take action against the concerned IT staff," the Court said. items.title: Problematic if choice of arbitrators can predict arbitration outcome: Justice Indu Malhotra
items.summary: It is deeply problematic if one can predict the outcome of an arbitration based on the composition of the arbitral tribunal, former Supreme Court Justice Indu Malhotra recently said. Justice Malhotra raised concerns over party-appointed arbitrators acting as partisans and warned against predictable decisions in multi-member tribunals. “That is something which I feel is a very serious matter of concern, because if you can predict the result from the constitution of the tribunal, it is problematic,” she said. She was speaking at a panel session during the India ADR Week 2026 in Mumbai. The discussion focused on conflicts, repeat appointments, and perceptions of bias. Advocates put forth the cause of the parties, and arbitrators should not be doing that, she opined. “You cannot expect the arbitrators to be taking a partisan view. They are not required to advocate the cause of the party. That is what I think is the biggest challenge to arbitration today,” she emphasised. items.title: TTD raises pilgrims’ accident cover to Rs 10 lakh, adds Rs 2 lakh life insurance
items.summary: The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) Board has approved a free life insurance cover of Rs 2 lakh for pilgrims who die of natural causes while visiting Tirumala, with the amount to be paid to their families. The TTD Board approved the proposal at its meeting in Tirumala on Wednesday, September 9, headed by chairman BR Naidu and attended by executive officer M Ravichandra. Naidu said the initiative would be the first of its kind among temple trusts in the country. Under the proposed scheme, the family of a pilgrim who dies of natural causes during their pilgrimage in Tirumala will receive Rs 2 lakh. TTD will bear the insurance premium. The initiative expands TTD’s existing accident insurance assistance for pilgrims. The Board also decided to increase the compensation for families of devotees who die in accidents in Tirumala from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 10 lakh. The existing assistance covers devotees killed in road accidents between Alipiri and Tirumala under specified circumstances. The decisions come ahead of the annual Salakatla Brahmotsavams of Lord Venkateswara, scheduled from September 15 to 23, when Tirumala is expected to see a substantial increase in the number of devotees.
